Actually, let me reconsider. The `FullProviders` wrapper gets applied when extras load. If one of the extra providers (Analytics, IPX, Wallet, Earn, Email, Network) throws during render, the `ProviderBoundary` catches it but maybe the error boundary itself has an issue, or maybe the re-mount caused by wrapping `AppStack` in `FullProviders` causes the navigation to reset.

Key insight: When `extras` goes from `null` to loaded, the entire tree changes from:
```
<EssentialProviders>
  <AppStack />
</EssentialProviders>
```
to:
```
<EssentialProviders>
  <FullProviders extras={extras}>
    <AppStack />
  </FullProviders>
</EssentialProviders>
```

This means `AppStack` gets unmounted and remounted inside a new set of providers. This would cause the entire navigation state to reset - the screen would flash and potentially go blank during the transition, especially if any of those providers have issues.

This is the bug. The transition from "no extras" to "extras loaded" causes a tree reshuffle that unmounts and remounts the entire navigation stack, causing the black screen.

The fix: Don't conditionally wrap AppStack. Instead, always render AppStack in the same position in the tree, and have the extra providers wrap from the outside but not change the tree structure. Or better yet, just render all providers synchronously but with error boundaries, and make the extras optional/non-blocking.

Actually, the simplest fix is to NOT change the tree structure when extras load. Instead of conditionally wrapping, we should either:

Let me think about this differently. The real problem is that the tree structure changes when extras load. The fix is to always keep AppStack in the same position in the tree, and have the extra providers wrap around it without changing its identity.
